## CAP-15 Logging, diagnostics and stats

`DittoLogger` is a set of process-wide static functions; the block is generated from a
test file that CI compiles:

<!-- snippet: rust-logging -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
async fn configure_logging() -> Result<(), DittoError> {
    // Process-wide; set before Ditto::open to cover start-up.
    DittoLogger::set_minimum_log_level(LogLevel::Warning);
    DittoLogger::set_custom_log_callback(|level, message| match level {
        LogLevel::Error => eprintln!("ditto error: {message}"),
        LogLevel::Warning => eprintln!("ditto warning: {message}"),
        _ => {}
    });
    // Gzipped JSON lines; the file must not exist yet.
    let bytes = DittoLogger::export_to_file("/tmp/ditto-logs.jsonl.gz").await?;
    println!("exported {bytes} bytes of logs");
    Ok(())
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `set_logging_enabled(bool)` / `get_logging_enabled()` | master switch |
| `set_minimum_log_level(LogLevel)` | `Error`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Debug`, `Verbose` |
| `set_custom_log_callback(Fn(LogLevel, &str) + Send + Sync + 'static)` | replaces console output for SDK log lines |
| `clear_custom_log_callback()` | |
| `export_to_file(path).await -> Result<u64>` | gzipped JSON lines; the file must not exist; use `.jsonl.gz` |

Observed (executed on 5.0.4–5.2.0):

- Ditto logs to **stderr** by default, at `Info`, in `tracing` format. Your stdout stays
  clean.
- The custom callback receives SDK log lines (executed: dozens of lines during open and
  sync start), but some lines from Ditto's discovery subsystem still reach stderr
  directly.
- The callback runs on whichever thread logged. A panic in it aborts the process, and
  calling Ditto APIs that log from inside it can re-enter it: keep it to formatting and
  forwarding.
- Use `LogLevel` from the prelude, not the re-exported `CLogLevel`.

## Routing logs into `tracing`

The SDK does not integrate with your `tracing` subscriber. Forward through the callback
(generated from a compiled test file; needs `tracing = "0.1"`):

<!-- snippet: rust-tracing-bridge -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
/// Forwards Ditto's log lines into the app's `tracing` subscriber.
fn forward_ditto_logs_to_tracing() {
    DittoLogger::set_custom_log_callback(|level, message| match level {
        LogLevel::Error => tracing::error!(target: "ditto", "{message}"),
        LogLevel::Warning => tracing::warn!(target: "ditto", "{message}"),
        LogLevel::Info => tracing::info!(target: "ditto", "{message}"),
        _ => tracing::debug!(target: "ditto", "{message}"),
    });
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

Do not let your subscriber call back into Ditto. Device logs for support are collected
with `export_to_file`; remote device observability is described at
<https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/deployment/logging>.

## Support bundles (5.2.0+)

A support bundle is a tar archive the device builds locally, offline, for Ditto Support:
logs, the effective configuration and runtime telemetry. Request it with DQL, then fetch
the archive through the attachment API. The block is generated from a test that CI runs
on 5.2.0 (on 5.0.x and 5.1.x the function does not exist and the call fails):

<!-- snippet: rust-support-bundle -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// Generates a support bundle (5.2.0+) and copies the archive to `destination`.
/// The bundle is a tar file stored as a local attachment; ship it to Ditto support
/// through your own channel.
async fn save_support_bundle(ditto: &Ditto, destination: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<PathBuf> {
    let result = ditto
        .store()
        .execute((
            "EXECUTE FUNCTION system_request_support_bundle({ 'metadata': :metadata })",
            json!({ "metadata": { "requested_by": "ops-cli" } }),
        ))
        .await?;
    let bundle = result
        .get_item(0)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("no bundle row"))?;
    let value = bundle.value();
    let token = value
        .get("file")
        .and_then(|file| file.as_object())
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("bundle row has no file"))?;

    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
    let tx = std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(tx));
    let _fetcher = ditto.store().fetch_attachment(token, move |event| {
        if let DittoAttachmentFetchEvent::Completed { attachment } = event {
            if let Some(tx) = tx.lock().ok().and_then(|mut slot| slot.take()) {
                let _ = tx.send(attachment.path());
            }
        }
    })?;
    let stored = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), rx).await??;
    std::fs::copy(&stored, destination)?; // never move or edit Ditto's own copy
    Ok(destination.to_path_buf())
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

- **Request:** `EXECUTE FUNCTION system_request_support_bundle()`, optionally with
  `{ 'metadata': { … } }`. It returns one row, `{ _id: { pk, created_at }, reason, file }`,
  in about 40 ms on an idle store (executed). `reason` is `USER_INITIATED`; `CRASH` marks
  bundles captured after a crash.
- **List:** `SELECT * FROM system:support_bundles ORDER BY _id.created_at DESC`. Bundles
  are retained locally: 10 by default, oldest evicted first.
- **Fetch:** `file` is an attachment token. Fetch it as in
  [attachments.md](attachments.md); copy the file, never move it.
- **Contents** (executed): `config_snapshot.json` (the `DittoConfig` with secrets
  redacted, every system parameter, the transport config, the SDK version),
  `ditto-logs.log.gz` (JSON-lines device logs at debug level, regardless of the console
  level), `device_logs_METADATA.json` (the log time range), and `dial9/dial9.bin.gz`
  once the process is older than a minute ([below](#dial9-runtime-telemetry)).
  `bundle_errors.txt` appears if a section failed.
- **Rate limit:** 3 requests per rolling 10 minutes per peer, counted on disk so it
  survives restarts. The fourth request fails (executed):
  `CoreApi(DqlEvaluationError)` "support bundle request rate exceeded: at most 3 requests
  are allowed per 10 minutes; retry in 600 seconds". Treat it as a user-facing
  "try later", not a retryable error. One bundle is generated at a time; a concurrent
  request is rejected, not queued.
- **Parameters:** `support_bundle_request_rate` (0 disables), `support_bundle_request_timeout`
  (seconds, default 30, max 3600) and `support_bundle_retention_limit` (default 10). Set
  them with `ALTER SYSTEM SET support_bundle_request_rate = 10` through `execute`, or in
  `DittoConfig.system_parameters` before `open`.
- **Where to expose it:** an admin endpoint, a CLI subcommand (`myapp support-bundle
  --out bundle.tar`) or a signal handler. Bundles requested from the device stay on the
  device until you ship them; bundles requested from the Ditto portal's device list
  upload to Ditto Server on their own (documented, not verified here).
- **Privacy:** the logs include full peer keys and absolute file paths. Review a bundle
  before attaching it to a public ticket.

Reference: <https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/deployment/support-bundles>.

## dial9 runtime telemetry

dial9 records the **Ditto core's internal Tokio runtime** (task polls, wakes, worker
parks) into an in-memory ring buffer, so Ditto Support can see executor starvation
inside the SDK. It does not instrument your application's runtime: for that, use
`tokio-console` or `tokio-metrics` on your own runtime.

| Control | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DITTO_DIAL9_OBSERVABILITY_LEVEL` | `0` off, `1` Lite, `2` Extended | `1` |
| `DITTO_DIAL9_BUFFER_SIZE_MB` | ≥ 1 | `16` |

- **These are process environment variables, read once** when Ditto first builds its
  runtime (source: `crates/dittoffi/src/runtime.rs` at `sdk-release-5.2.0`). Set them in
  the service unit, container spec or shell — not in `DittoConfig`, which is read after
  the runtime exists. The start-up log confirms the value:
  `dittoffi: initializing dial9 async tracing dial9.observability_level=Lite`.
- **The first 60 seconds produce no trace.** Segments rotate every 60 s, and a bundle
  includes only completed segments. Executed on 5.2.0: bundles taken 1–15 s after start
  have no `dial9/` entry (macOS arm64; Linux x86_64 and aarch64); one taken after 75 s
  carries a 517 KB `dial9/dial9.bin.gz` (macOS arm64). A bundle for a start-up problem therefore needs a process
  that keeps running for over a minute.
- Extended (`2`) adds CPU profiling only in builds with Ditto's `dial9-cpu-profiling`
  feature. Executed: setting `2` is accepted ("system parameter default overridden
  … value=U64(2)"); whether the published Rust library includes CPU profiling was not
  verified.
- Lite is intended to be left on. Turn it off (`0`) only to rule out its overhead, and
  size the buffer down on memory-constrained hosts.
- The `.bin.gz` is for Ditto Support's tooling; there is no public decoder.

## Disk usage

<!-- snippet: rust-disk-usage -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
fn report_disk_usage(ditto: &Ditto) -> std::sync::Arc<DiskUsageObserverHandle> {
    println!(
        "store size: {} bytes",
        ditto.disk_usage().item().size_in_bytes
    );
    // Unlike store observers, dropping this handle stops the observation.
    ditto.disk_usage().observe(|usage: DiskUsageItem| {
        println!("store size now: {} bytes", usage.size_in_bytes);
    })
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

`DiskUsageItem { fs_type, path, size_in_bytes, children }` is a tree rooted at the
persistence directory. Unlike store observers, dropping the `DiskUsageObserverHandle`
stops the observation (source: `src/disk_usage/mod.rs`). Executed: `item()` reports a
non-zero size right after the first write.

## Small peer info

`ditto.small_peer_info()` controls the device metadata Ditto publishes to the
`__small_peer_info` collection: `set_enabled(bool)` (default on),
`set_sync_scope(DittoSmallPeerInfoSyncScope::BigPeerOnly | LocalPeerOnly)` (default
`BigPeerOnly`), and `set_metadata(&impl Serialize)` (128 KB, 64 levels). It is how a
device appears in the Ditto portal's device dashboards:
<https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/deployment/device-observability-and-ditto-logs>.
